title: jwks_auth plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `jwks_auth` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component JwksAuthConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

JwksAuthConfig.description: Plugin: jwks_auth — Multi-provider JWKS JWT validation with claim-based authorization. JWT header kid is required and binding: a missing, empty, or unknown kid is rejected with a generic 401. There is no all-keys fallback; a known kid selects only that trusted key. A token is verified only against providers whose issuer equals its unverified iss claim, then providers that configure no issuer; providers pinning a different issuer are never tried. At most 64 providers are allowed, and for every issuer the providers sharing it plus the providers without an issuer must total at most 8 (at most 8 may omit issuer). A provider without an issuer never authenticates a token whose verified iss is the issuer of a provider in the same instance that requires DPoP or mTLS binding, so it cannot strip that realm's sender constraint. Verified algorithms: RS256/RS384/RS512, PS256/PS384/PS512, ES256/ES384, and EdDSA (Ed25519 OKP keys; refused while FIPS mode is enforced). ES512 is not supported. Verification is bound to the selected JWK's alg (an RSA JWK without alg is RS256).

jwks_uri.description: Direct URL to the IdP's JWKS endpoint. HTTPS is required except for a loopback IP-literal host (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1]); the name localhost does not qualify, because DNS overrides and the resolver decide where a name connects. URL userinfo is rejected. Exactly one of jwks_uri, discovery_url, jwks, or jwks_source may be configured per provider.

discovery_url.description: OIDC discovery URL (auto-discovers jwks_uri). The discovered jwks_uri must use the same origin as the discovery URL (scheme, host, and effective port). For IdPs that serve JWKS from a different origin than discovery, configure jwks_uri directly instead. HTTPS is required except for a loopback IP-literal host (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1]); the name localhost does not qualify. URL userinfo is rejected. After the first successful resolution, discovery is re-run every jwks_refresh_interval_secs; a changed jwks_uri is adopted once its key set has usable keys, otherwise the last-known-good store is retained.

jwks.description: Inline JWKS JSON string or object

jwks_source.description: Admin-managed JWKS record: `managed://jwks/<id>#jwks` (also accepted: `managed://jwks/<id>`, `managed://<id>#jwks`, and the `#jwks-json` / `#jwks_json` fragment aliases), stored through `/admin/tls/jwks`. Exactly one of jwks_uri, discovery_url, jwks, or jwks_source may be configured per provider. Only the `managed://` scheme is accepted; a fragment or collection that selects other material, `?` options, and an invalid record id are refused at config load. The record is read from this node's managed TLS store (`FERRUM_TLS_MANAGED_STORE_PATH`): while it is present and holds a usable signing key the key set is fresh; once it is deleted, of another kind, or keyless every key is withdrawn and tokens are refused (like an expired remote set); a store that cannot be read keeps the last-read keys in grace for at most jwks_max_stale_seconds. The record is re-read every jwks_refresh_interval_secs, on an unknown kid (subject to kid_miss_refresh_cooldown_seconds), and immediately after a local `/admin/tls/jwks` write. Admin writes refuse a reference to a record that does not exist; file mode refuses to start without it; database mode warns. Namespace-bounded operator tokens may not introduce one.

issuer.description: Expected JWT iss claim — routes tokens to this provider. When set, the token MUST carry iss and it must match exactly; the issuer check alone rejects only a mismatching claim. Per RFC 7519 section 4.1.1 a present iss must be a single string: an array, object, number, boolean, or null iss is rejected even when one element matches this value. Required and must be nonblank when require_dpop is true: the DPoP replay realm is this exact issuer, so key-set or JWKS source rotation cannot reopen a proof. Issuers are compared exactly and are not URL-canonicalized. Providers in one policy that share this exact issuer share one replay realm and must agree on require_dpop; when DPoP is required they must also agree on dpop_replay_scope and, for process scope, dpop_replay_max_entries. A non-DPoP sibling for the same issuer is refused as a bearer-only bypass.

audiences.description: Accepted JWT aud claims; OR matched. No entry may be blank. When non-empty the token MUST carry aud and at least one value must match. When empty, tokens without aud are accepted and a token that carries aud is rejected because no acceptable audience is configured (RFC 7519 4.1.3).

name.description: Header name to read the token from; must be a valid HTTP header name (surrounding whitespace is trimmed)

prefix.description: Optional token prefix to strip; an empty string or null is treated as no prefix

from_params.description: Custom query parameter token locations; no entry may be blank

forward_original_token.description: Whether to forward the token-bearing header or query parameter upstream

require_exp.description: Per-provider override for requiring an exp claim. Expiry is always validated when present. A present nbf is always validated too (it is not required). exp is an RFC 7519 section 2 NumericDate (a JSON number that may carry a fractional part); a fractional exp bounds the authenticated stream exactly like an integer one, truncated toward the past so the enforced expiry is never later than the token states. nbf presence and validation are delegated to the JWT validation layer; Ferrum does not normalize a fractional nbf. JWT exp/nbf use the effective clock_skew_seconds leeway (default 0); DPoP skew is a separate proof contract.

required_scopes.description: Scopes that must all be present in the token; no entry may be blank. Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer must declare the same list and, when it is non-empty, the same effective scope_claim.

required_roles.description: Roles where any one must be present; no entry may be blank. Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer must declare the same list and, when it is non-empty, the same effective role_claim.

scope_claim.description: Per-provider override for scope claim path. A dot path with no empty segments. Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer and require scopes must resolve to the same effective path.

role_claim.description: Per-provider override for role claim path. A dot path with no empty segments. Same equivalence requirement as scope_claim.

consumer_identity_claim.description: Per-provider override for the external authenticated identity claim (falls back to global); a dot path with no empty segments. The identity is never resolved to a gateway Consumer.

consumer_header_claim.description: Per-provider override for X-Authenticated-Identity claim (falls back to global, then to this provider's effective consumer_identity_claim); a dot path with no empty segments

claim_headers.description: Per-provider claim path to upstream header mappings. Destination headers are gateway-owned and always sanitized: every configured destination is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before verified claim values are installed, so an absent, null, empty, or wrong-type claim leaves the header absent instead of forwarding client-supplied input. Destinations in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace and `x-authenticated-identity` are rejected at config load. At most 16 mappings; claim paths are at most 256 bytes with no whitespace or control characters, header names at most 128 bytes, and two mappings may not name the same header. Framing, provenance, credential-bearing and gateway-reserved destinations (including cookie, content-length, forwarded, via, x-real-ip, x-forwarded-* and x-ferrum-*) are rejected, as for output_claim_headers. In both forms reserved names and duplicates are matched case-insensitively with _ treated as - (X_Real_IP is reserved, X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, including across jwks_auth claim_headers and output_claim_headers). A claim value that is not a valid header value (for example one containing CR or LF) or that renders to more than 8192 bytes, including a joined array, leaves the destination absent.

claim_headers_separator.description: Separator for array claim header values; must not be empty

header.description: Backend-visible request header the claim is published to; must be a valid HTTP header name. Reserved, framing, provenance, and credential-bearing destinations are additionally rejected at config load (the closed list is not expressible as a pattern).

claim.description: Dot-path claim to publish; no empty segments, and no whitespace or control characters

output_claim_headers.description: Istio RequestAuthentication jwtRules[].outputClaimToHeaders projection. An ordered list rather than a map, because one claim may be published to several headers. Destinations are gateway-owned exactly like claim_headers: each is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before validation and set only from a validated claim, so an unauthenticated or invalid request can never forge one. Duplicate destination headers, reserved/credential-bearing destinations, and invalid header names are rejected at config load; names are compared with _ treated as - (X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, X_Real_IP is reserved). Only nonblank string, integer, and boolean claims are published (Istio ClaimToHeader does not support arrays, objects, null, or floating-point numbers); anything else or a header-illegal value leaves the destination absent. A rendered claim value over 8192 bytes is omitted before fan-out.

require_mtls_binding.description: Require cnf.x5t#S256 to match the frontend client certificate. A provider without an issuer never authenticates a token whose iss is this provider's issuer. A provider that sets this without an issuer is admitted only when every provider in the instance also sets it; otherwise the configuration is rejected, because an unbound sibling could accept its tokens without the certificate.

require_dpop.description: Require and validate an RFC 9449 DPoP proof. Requires a nonblank exact issuer (the replay realm) and dpop_replay_scope, because an accepted proof must be made single-use against a declared replay authority. The access token is accepted under either the DPoP (RFC 9449 7.1) or Bearer authorization scheme, and the DPoP scheme is matched only against providers that set this flag. Validated proof claims are htm, htu, iat, jti and ath (RFC 9449 4.2); exp is not an RFC 9449 proof claim and is not required, but a proof that carries one is rejected once it has passed. The proof htu path is canonicalized exactly like the request path (percent-encoded pchar escapes decoded), so a proof bound to the URI the client sent matches. Proofs may be signed with ES256/ES384, RS256/RS384/RS512, PS256/PS384/PS512, or EdDSA (Ed25519; refused while FIPS mode is enforced). Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer must agree on this flag; matching order would otherwise let a sibling skip the proof. A provider without an issuer never authenticates a token whose iss is this provider's issuer.

dpop_clock_skew_secs.description: DPoP proof clock skew allowance in seconds, applied to iat (and to exp when a client sends the non-standard claim). Bounded because the fixed replay retention horizon (601s) is derived from twice this ceiling, so no reload can shorten an already-admitted proof's protection.

dpop_replay_scope.description: Required when require_dpop is true; there is no default. Use 'shared' together with sync_mode 'redis' for any deployment running more than one gateway replica: every replica then claims each proof through one atomic Redis SET NX EX. Use 'process' to declare a single-process deployment whose replay protection is stable across equivalent reloads but explicitly not cross-replica. There is no fallback between them — a shared-backend timeout, partition, authentication failure, or capacity failure rejects the protected request. Equivalent DPoP providers that share a replay domain must declare the same value; a mixed process/shared pair is refused even when Redis is configured, because matching order would otherwise claim the same proof once in the process store and once in Redis.

dpop_replay_max_entries.description: Capacity this process-scoped authority enforces against the shared replay lane. At capacity only expired markers are reclaimed; if none can be, the request is refused (503) rather than a live marker evicted. Repeated full-live refusals are O(1) until an expiry is actually due. An equivalent reload applies the new cap without forgetting live markers. Duplicate equivalent providers that share a replay domain must declare the same value. Ignored for 'shared'.

jwks_max_stale_seconds.description: Per-provider maximum monotonic age of the last validated non-empty remote JWKS. Overrides the plugin default. Zero is invalid and cannot disable bounded stale-key expiry. Applies to jwks_uri, discovery_url, and jwks_source sources (for a managed record it bounds how long the last-read keys survive an unreadable store); supplying it on an inline jwks provider is rejected. jwks_refresh_interval_secs must not exceed this value — a cross-field rule JSON Schema cannot express, enforced at config load.

clock_skew_seconds.description: Per-provider JWT exp/nbf clock leeway in seconds; overrides the plugin-level clock_skew_seconds. The authenticated-stream deadline is exp plus this leeway.

scope_claim.description: Global scope claim path; a dot path with no empty segments

role_claim.description: Global role claim path; a dot path with no empty segments

consumer_identity_claim.description: JWT claim used as the external authenticated identity; a dot path with no empty segments. The identity is scoped to the provider that verified it and is never resolved to a gateway Consumer (not by username, id, or custom_id), so Consumer-scoped policy does not apply to jwks_auth principals.

consumer_header_claim.description: JWT claim for X-Authenticated-Identity header (defaults to each provider's effective consumer_identity_claim); a dot path with no empty segments

claim_headers.description: Global claim path to upstream header mappings. Destination headers are gateway-owned and always sanitized: every configured destination is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before verified claim values are installed, so an absent, null, empty, or wrong-type claim leaves the header absent instead of forwarding client-supplied input. Destinations in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace and `x-authenticated-identity` are rejected at config load. At most 16 mappings; claim paths are at most 256 bytes with no whitespace or control characters, header names at most 128 bytes, and two mappings may not name the same header. Framing, provenance, credential-bearing and gateway-reserved destinations (including cookie, content-length, forwarded, via, x-real-ip, x-forwarded-* and x-ferrum-*) are rejected, as for output_claim_headers. In both forms reserved names and duplicates are matched case-insensitively with _ treated as - (X_Real_IP is reserved, X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, including across jwks_auth claim_headers and output_claim_headers). A claim value that is not a valid header value (for example one containing CR or LF) or that renders to more than 8192 bytes, including a joined array, leaves the destination absent.

claim_headers_separator.description: Separator for array claim header values; must not be empty

emit_mesh_request_principal_metadata.description: Emits mesh.request_principal plus mesh JWT claim/audience metadata for direct mesh_authz request-principal and when-condition evaluation. Metadata only; it never relaxes authentication.

allow_missing_token.description: Istio RequestAuthentication semantics. When true and this is the only applicable auth plugin, a request carrying no token is forwarded UNAUTHENTICATED (an invalid token is still rejected). Mesh mode sets this on its generated RequestAuthentication instance; leave it false on a standalone gateway unless optional authentication is intended.

require_exp.description: Global default for requiring an exp claim

clock_skew_seconds.description: JWT exp/nbf clock leeway in seconds for every provider without its own clock_skew_seconds. The authenticated-stream deadline is exp plus the effective leeway, never later. DPoP proof skew is the separate dpop_clock_skew_secs.

jwks_refresh_interval_secs.description: JWKS key refresh interval in seconds. Must not exceed the effective jwks_max_stale_seconds for any remote provider. discovery_url providers also re-run OIDC discovery at this interval.

jwks_max_stale_seconds.description: Maximum monotonic age of the last validated non-empty remote JWKS. Cached keys fail closed at this deadline even if refreshes keep failing or return empty. Zero is invalid and cannot disable expiry.

kid_miss_refresh_cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum spacing between out-of-band JWKS refetches triggered by a token naming a kid the trusted key set does not contain — the observable shape of an identity-provider key rotation. At most one fetch is issued per window, so tokens carrying random identifiers cannot become a fetch storm. The triggering request is never blocked on the fetch and still fails closed; a later request verifies once the refreshed key set is published. A token with a missing or empty kid triggers nothing. Zero disables the on-demand refetch, leaving jwks_refresh_interval_secs as the only recovery path. Shared stores use the most restrictive value requested by active consumers (disabled wins, otherwise the longest cooldown).

sync_mode.description: DPoP replay-marker storage. 'redis' is required by (and only valid with) at least one provider declaring dpop_replay_scope 'shared'; it is what makes DPoP replay protection cross-replica. Any RESP-compatible single-endpoint server works (Redis Cluster is not supported and is screened, not assumed).

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL with a redis:// or rediss:// scheme and a non-empty authority/hostname. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for shared DPoP replay markers. Must be non-empty when supplied. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:jwks_auth:{plugin-config-id}`, which isolates independent policies inside a namespace while keeping every replica of one policy claiming against the same keyspace. An explicit prefix is the opt-in for deliberately sharing a keyspace across policies.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be greater than zero.
